title: Three-bar plane truss on an inclined roller

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Pin-jointed plane truss in the x-y plane (global Y vertical): members of type 'truss'; the out-of-plane translation of every joint is held by a support (it has no stiffness in a plane truss). Truss of Example 3.2 (c (0, 0), a (4/tan 30 deg, 4), b (4/tan 30 deg + 4, 0) m; A_ac = 15e3, A_ab = 20e3, A_bc = 18e3 mm^2; E = 200,000 MPa; load at a 383.0 kN in x and 321.4 kN in y), c pinned, b on a roller whose plane is inclined 30 deg to the x axis. The input format has supports along global axes only. The model is therefore written in the source's joint axes x'', y'' of b: every coordinate and the load are rotated by -30 deg, so that the roller plane is the model's X axis and the roller holds uy at b. The rotation of the data is exact; the structure is the same. Only the displacement the source gives in these axes (u_b'') can be compared without transforming printed values; the source's u_a = 0.928 mm and v_a = 1.143 mm (global axes) are not targets (the engine gives 0.9282 and 1.1425 mm after rotating its result back, see README.md). First order.

targets.precisionNote: printed "0.094"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; printed -0.094 (u_b'' along the inclined plane)
targets.sign: the model's X axis is the source's joint axis x'' at b
